children: China's consumer price index likely rise on food prices, according to BofA Securities in a research note. CPI inflation is likely to rise to 0.7% on year in August, from 0.5% in July, supported by a favorable base effect, the bank says. Food prices should provide the main push up, with vegetable prices rising 6.6% on month amid weather-related supply disruptions, they say. Another positive factor is pork prices, which likely increased due to seasonal factors and structural shifts, they say.(tracy.qu@wsj.com)
